RUSSIAN ROULETTE - C48 PILOT CHECKPOINT

New C48 source: src/roulette.c
ZX-UX executable: bin/ssx/roulette.ssx
Native ZX-UX cassette: bin/tzx/roulette.tzx, on-tape name roulette

Controls: A advances the six-chamber cylinder, B fires, Q quits.
One chamber is live. Firing another scores 100 points. A shot in the
live chamber resets the current score and updates the highest score.
RVM replay --keys '{WAIT 80}aaab' produces a survival result with 100.
RVM replay --keys '{WAIT 80}b' produces the live-chamber result.
Native FUSE replays:
    python3 -B tools/bonus_fuse.py --case roulette:intro [...]
    python3 -B tools/bonus_fuse.py --case roulette:result [...]
The command's --help lists the required host paths and switches.

Visual review: original BASIC 01-READY and 02-SURVIVAL-RESULT compared
with real C48 RVM and native FUSE captures. Six chamber circles, the
revolver outline, instructions, and 100-point survival result are visible.
Original C48 text uses the required ZX-UX font64; spacing differs.

Known difference: one A keypress advances one chamber, whereas the
original BASIC cycles chambers while A remains held. Game outcome,
score accounting and the live chamber are retained. This difference
must be considered before claiming full input timing parity.

Native FUSE and RVM runs were performed using the real ZX-UX kernel.
See tests/test_bonus_pilots.py for executable replay checks.
